title: [POSTMORTEM] Alien Orbit Assault — How five AI tools built a Toaplan-style shmup
author: kc00l76
selftext:
Alien Orbit Assault is a vertical shmup built using five AI tools for different parts of the pipeline. This spread breaks down the workflow, the tools we relied on, and critically — where we still needed human judgment.  
  
First devlog of many: [https://kc00l.itch.io/alien-orbital-assault/devlog/1507177/one-boss-no-waves-no-regrets](https://kc00l.itch.io/alien-orbital-assault/devlog/1507177/one-boss-no-waves-no-regrets)  
Play it here: [https://kc00l.itch.io/alien-orbital-assault](https://kc00l.itch.io/alien-orbital-assault)  
  
Questions? Happy to dive into the design decisions.

comments.author: kc00l76
comments.body: Not my first AI assisted game, but maybe the most complete and polished. My background: semi-pro fullstack web dev, passion and obsession for good and optimized code.

comments.author: Sebguer
comments.body: I highly recommend that you take the time to actually write the copy yourself for something like this, or get better at prompting away the AI-isms. As-is, it's unreadable slop and kills any interest I might have in the game.

replies.author: kc00l76
replies.body:
Thanks for the reply. I'm curious, is it the format or the AI ism which contributes to the slop? I haven't rewritten all the text but I made sure it was relevant to the game and to the development workflow.
Also, would a more graphical postmortem have helped?

replies.author: Sebguer
replies.body:
It's the AI-ism, the format would be \~fine if the words did not sound so clearly like Claude. (Though the color scheme and the drop quote also are a bit much, I can understandt he aesthetic you were going for). 

The worst line was:

"The whole stack is AI-native. The whole feel is mine." 

Because this completely at odds with the feel being yours! You didn't even take the time to write the copy!

comments.author: MightyBig-Dev
comments.body: Very cool and good write up. Kudos

comments.author: Able_Zombie_7859
comments.body: This document doesn't actually say much at all, it's pretty scatterbrained and assumes a lot of things that only you know, really limited in useful with regards to your infographic, it's reads like retroencabulator talk. Just like a good coding agent, we need a lot more context to be able to make anything of this.
